transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I keep getting stuck on these ideas that people around me are plotting or judging me, even when they swear they aren’t. My wife, our pastor, and my primary doctor all strongly suggested I come in and talk to someone, so I reluctantly agreed to make an appointment. It's just really hard to shake the feeling that something is going on behind my back.
Can you tell me more about these ideas that people are plotting or judging you, are they fleeting thoughts or do you strongly believe them to be true even when others contradict you?

They definitely aren't fleeting; they feel incredibly real and are so hard to shake. For instance, when my supervisor moved me off a big EV job, both he and my husband swore they hadn't talked, but I still can't shake the strong feeling that they're planning things behind my back.
Do you ever hear voices or see things that others can't, or are these suspicions based solely on your interpretations of what people say or do?

Yes, I actually do hear a man's voice sometimes when I'm alone in the garage late at night, saying things like "They're laughing at you" even though I know no one is actually there. And the suspicions are definitely more than just misinterpreting things; I still have this intense, unshakable feeling that people are actively plotting against me behind my back.
Can you describe more about the voice you hear, such as how often it occurs, what kind of things it says, and whether it seems to be responding to your thoughts or commenting on your surroundings?

I hear a man's voice clear as day, usually when I'm alone in the house or working late at the garage, and it comments on whatever I'm doing with things like, "They're laughing at you" or "You're wasting your time." Even though I know there's no one actually there, it feels completely real to me. This has been happening on and off like this since late last fall.
Do you feel that the voice you hear is part of these plots you suspect, or is it a separate experience that you're having?

They feel closely connected because when the voice says things like "They're laughing at you," it just reinforces my feeling that people are judging me or setting me up to fail. Even though it happens when I'm completely alone, it feels like it's confirming that those plots behind my back are actually happening.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your mood, such as feeling excessively sad, empty, or irritable, in addition to these experiences with the voice and the suspicions of plotting?

Yes, my mood has been all over the place lately. Some days I feel on top of the world, full of energy and talking a mile a minute, but then I'll get incredibly irritable and snap at my wife or coworkers over the smallest comment. In the moment it feels like they are attacking me, though I usually realize later that I overreacted.

Can you tell me if there are periods where you don't experience these voices or suspicious thoughts, and during those times, do you feel like your normal self, or are you still struggling with mood swings or other unusual feelings?

The voices and suspicious feelings have been around most of the time since last fall, and even if they quiet down briefly, I rarely feel normal because I'm usually caught up in those wired, high-energy phases or recovering from them. In fact, this past spring my mood completely flattened out and I wasn't feeling high or low, but I still kept hearing that man's voice and felt convinced people were plotting against me during those weeks.
Can you estimate how long these high-energy phases typically last, and do they seem to be triggered by anything in particular, or do they just happen spontaneously?

These high-energy phases have been coming and going for close to a year now, dominating most of my time with only brief normal periods in between. The overall issues started building up about a year and a few months ago from the stress of planning for a baby and taking on extra EV training at the shop. Now, though, the individual phases just seem to come and go on their own.

Can you clarify if the voices and suspicious thoughts are always present, even during your high-energy phases, or if they tend to fade into the background when you're feeling particularly energetic or manic?

Yes, they are definitely present during those high-energy phases. In fact, when I first started staying late at the shop with all that energy, barely sleeping and taking on extra projects, that was exactly when the voice kicked in and I became convinced my coworkers and wife were plotting to undermine me.

Do you find that your suspicious thoughts and the voice you hear are more pronounced or intense during your high-energy phases, or do they remain relatively consistent regardless of your mood and energy level?

They definitely kick in very strongly when I'm in those high-energy, sleep-deprived phases. However, they aren't exclusive to those times; this past spring, my mood flattened out completely, but I still heard the voice and felt people were plotting against me for a few weeks without any of that high energy.

Can you estimate the total duration of a typical cycle from the start of a high-energy phase, through any potential low or normal periods, and back to another high-energy phase, and how these cycles have been affecting your daily life and relationships?

These high-energy periods have been coming and going for close to a year, and I'm usually either in one of those wired phases or coming down from it, with only very brief normal breaks. It has taken a massive toll on my life because my wife and I fight constantly, my supervisor cut my work responsibilities after we argued, and I've completely stopped going to my car club or keeping up with bills and chores at home.

Have you ever experienced a period where the voices stopped and the suspicious thoughts significantly decreased or disappeared for a while, and if so, how did your mood and energy levels change during those times?

To be honest, I haven't really had a period where the voices and suspicious thoughts stopped or went away; they've been pretty constant and hanging around most of the time since late last fall. Because they've been so persistent, I haven't actually experienced a time where they disappeared to see how my mood or energy would change.

Can you describe how the intensity of the voice and your suspicious thoughts compare to the intensity of your mood swings, and do they seem to be directly related to each other or separate experiences?

Initially, they felt very tied together because the voice and suspicions kicked in really strongly during my high-energy phase when I was staying late at the shop and barely sleeping. However, they also happen independently, like this past spring when my mood flattened out but I still heard the voice and felt plotted against for a few weeks without any high energy.
Do you think the voices and suspicious thoughts are more distressing or disruptive to your life than the mood swings and high-energy phases, or are they equally bothersome to you?

They are honestly equally bothersome to me because they both disrupt my life in different ways. The voices and suspicious thoughts isolate me and cause constant conflicts at work and home, while the high-energy phases lead to exhaustion, racing thoughts, and severe strain on my marriage. Since they overlap so much, both sides of it feel incredibly distressing.

When you're experiencing a high-energy phase and also hearing the voice or having suspicious thoughts, do you feel like the voice or thoughts are more in control, or do you feel like you're still able to make decisions and act based on your own desires during those times?
I'm not quite sure how to describe who is in control during those times. Everything happens so fast and feels so intense that I don't really stop to think about who is making the decisions.

When you're in a high-energy phase, do the voices and suspicious thoughts seem to be directly related to your elevated mood, or do they seem to be separate experiences that can occur regardless of your mood?

They definitely happen together, because when I first started having those high-energy phases with barely any sleep, that was exactly when the voice and the paranoid thoughts really kicked in. But they also happen completely on their own; this past spring, my mood flattened out and I wasn't feeling up or down, but I still heard the voice and believed people were plotting against me for a few weeks.

Can you think of any times when the voices or suspicious thoughts completely stopped, even briefly, without any change in your mood or energy levels, which might help us understand their relationship better?

No, they haven't really ever completely stopped. Even during a stretch last spring when my mood and energy levels had flattened out and felt relatively normal, I still kept hearing the voice and feeling like people were plotting against me for a few weeks.
Do you think the voices and suspicious thoughts are always present, even when you're not in a high-energy phase, or do they tend to occur only during or immediately after these phases?

Yes, they definitely happen even when I'm not in a high-energy phase. For instance, this past spring my mood had mostly flattened out and I wasn't feeling particularly "up" or "down," but I still heard the man's voice and felt convinced people at work were plotting against me for a few weeks.

Can you clarify if there are times when the voices and suspicious thoughts are present without any significant mood changes, and if so, how you experience those times differently from the times when they occur with high-energy phases or mood swings?

Yes, during that stretch last spring, my mood was completely flat and I wasn't feeling high or low, but I still heard the man's voice and felt convinced people were plotting against me. The difference was that I didn't have the racing thoughts, extra energy, or the urge to stay up late working, but the unsettling voices and suspicions remained just as real.

Have you ever experienced any periods where the voices completely stopped and you didn't have any suspicious thoughts for an extended period, even if your mood was stable or you were in a low-energy phase?

No, those voices and suspicious thoughts haven't really stopped for any long stretch, and they've been hanging around most of the time since late last fall. Even during a period last spring when my mood had flattened out and I wasn't feeling high-energy or down, I still kept hearing the voice and believing people were plotting against me.

When you're experiencing a period of intense suspiciousness or hearing the voice, do you feel like you're able to recognize that these thoughts or the voice might not be based in reality, or do they feel completely real to you at the time?

The suspicious thoughts feel completely real and unshakeable at the time, even when my wife and supervisor swear that none of it is true. As for the voice, while I logically know deep down that nobody is physically in the room, it sounds incredibly clear and real in the moment, making it very hard to ignore.

During these episodes of suspicious thoughts and hearing voices, are you ever able to step back and think that these experiences might not be real, or do they always feel completely real and true to you?

They almost always feel completely real to me, and it is incredibly hard to shake the suspicious thoughts even when others assure me they aren't true. As for the voice, even though I intellectually know no one is physically there, it still sounds so clear and real in the moment that I can't help but react to it.

When you are not in a high-energy phase and the voice is telling you that people are plotting against you, can you think of any situation or evidence that would make you question or doubt the voice's claims?

Even when my mood is flat and my husband and supervisor reassure me that nothing is going on, I still can't shake the feeling of being plotted against. While I logically know there isn't a physical person there when I hear the voice, the belief itself feels incredibly real. Because of that, it is really hard to find any situation or evidence that actually makes me doubt what I'm experiencing.
When the voice tells you that people are plotting against you, are you able to consider the possibility that the voice might be wrong, or do you always believe what it says?

Even though I rationally know there isn't a physical person there speaking to me, in the moment it feels incredibly real and I can't shake the feeling that what the voice says is true. Despite everyone telling me otherwise, I find it almost impossible not to believe that people are actually plotting against or judging me.
Can you describe if the voices or suspicious thoughts ever involve themes of grandiosity, such as feeling specially gifted or having a special mission, in addition to the plots against you?

The voices themselves are usually just critical or mocking, but during my up phases, I definitely get strong thoughts of being specially gifted. I get convinced that I'm the only one at the shop who truly understands the new EV systems and that I'm meant to completely change how the whole place runs. It feels like I see a much bigger picture that everyone else is just too small-minded to grasp.
Can you tell me more about these feelings of being specially gifted during your high-energy phases, such as how often they occur and how they relate to your suspicions of plotting against you?

During these high-energy phases, which have been coming and going for close to a year, I feel uniquely gifted and truly believe I'm the only one who understands the new EV systems and should run the training program. When I'm in these high states, my suspicions and the voices kick in at the exact same time. It makes me feel like my supervisor and husband are actively plotting to undermine me and hold me back because they don't trust me or my abilities.
Can you describe in more detail how these feelings of being specially gifted relate to your overall sense of self and your interactions with others, especially during your high-energy phases?

During those high-energy phases, I feel incredibly capable and genuinely believe I'm the only one at the shop who truly understands the new EV systems, like I see a "bigger picture" that everyone else is too small-minded to grasp. Because of this, I feel like management should just hand the training program over to me, which really strains my interactions since I get easily frustrated and snap at my coworkers or supervisor when they don't see things my way.

Can you help me understand how your feelings of being specially gifted and your suspicions of people plotting against you relate to each other, and whether one seems to trigger the other or if they feel like separate experiences to you?

They definitely feel connected because when I'm in those high-energy phases feeling uniquely capable with the EV systems, that is exactly when I also feel convinced people are plotting to undermine me and I hear the voice. However, they can also happen separately. For instance, this past spring my mood flattened out and I didn't feel that high energy or special confidence at all, but I still had those suspicious thoughts and heard the voice for a few weeks.
Can you describe any instances where your feelings of being specially gifted led to actions or decisions that you later regretted or that caused problems in your relationships or work?

Yes, believing I was the only one who truly understood the new EV systems made me feel I should run the training program, which led to a major conflict with my supervisor. I argued with him because I felt he and the others were too small-minded to see the bigger picture. Because of that argument, he ended up cutting back my responsibilities at the shop.

Can you describe if there are times when you feel so specially gifted or have such a strong sense of grandiosity that it leads you to do things that put you or others at risk, or if these feelings are more contained and don't influence your actions in significant ways?

I don't think I do things that are physically risky, but those feelings of being the only one who truly understands the EV systems definitely influence my actions. They make me clash with my supervisor because I feel others are too small-minded, which ended up hurting my job standing and getting my responsibilities cut back.
